title: Clear defining equations and the inverse-Jacobian certificate while retaining the localized kernel
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, p a prime ideal, R_p its localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and D an R_p-algebra with compatible R-algebra structure. Let n,m,c be natural numbers with c ≤ n+m, and P a submersive presentation of D over R_p on n+m variables and c equations whose selected variables are the first c [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. There exist f_j ∈ R[x_1,…,x_{n+m}], s ∈ R \\ p and h ∈ R[x_1,…,x_{n+m}] such that C(s)-h det(∂f_j/∂x_i)_{i,j≤c} belongs to (f_j), every f_j evaluates to zero at P.val, and extension of the ideal (f_j) to R_p[x_1,…,x_{n+m}] is exactly the kernel of evaluation at P.val. Polynomial rings and derivatives are those of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), lines 2179–2188, clearing the equations, inverse determinant, and relations

proof.text: Install MvPolynomial.algebraMvPolynomial. Mathlib MvPolynomial.isLocalization identifies the coefficient map φ with localization at M = C(R \ p). For each relation apply IsLocalization.surj M and extract its constant denominator, obtaining f_j and s_j outside p with φ(f_j) = C(s_j/1) P.relation j. IsLocalization.map_units shows each multiplying constant is a unit.

Evaluate the clearing equality and use Presentation.aeval_val_relation and MvPolynomial.aeval_map_algebraMap to prove f_j vanishes. Rewrite Ideal.map_span and compare the two generated ideals. One containment follows by evaluation; for the other multiply P.relation j by its unit constant and use Ideal.unit_mul_mem_iff_mem and Presentation.span_range_relation_eq_ker.

Use MvPolynomial.pderiv_map and pderiv_C_mul entrywise, and hmap to identify the selected coordinates. RingHom.map_det and Matrix.det_mul_row show φ(Δ) = (product_j C(s_j/1)) det(P.jacobiMatrix). Evaluate, identify the second factor with P.jacobian using jacobian_eq_jacobiMatrix_det and algebraMap_eq, and apply P.jacobian_isUnit and IsUnit.prod_univ_iff. Empty products and the empty determinant are handled by these same general identities.

Choose an inverse v of the evaluated determinant and lift it to q through P.aeval_val_surjective. Apply IsLocalization.surj M to q to get a polynomial h and t outside p with q C(t/1) = φ(h). Evaluation and the inverse identity prove φ(C(t)-h Δ) belongs to the localized kernel, hence to Ideal.map φ (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).

Apply Mathlib IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff to this membership to get r outside p with C(r)(C(t)-h Δ) in (f). Set s = rt and replace h by C(r)h. Closure of the prime complement under products proves s is outside p; map_mul for C and ring normalize the ideal certificate. Return this certificate with the already proved vanishing and localized-kernel equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_cleared_submersive_presentation_core
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    {D : Type v} [CommRing D] [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) D]
    [Algebra R D] [IsScalarTower R (Localization.AtPrime p) D]
    (n m c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ n + m)
    (P : SubmersivePresentation (Localization.AtPrime p) D (Fin (n + m)) (Fin c))
    (hmap : P.map = Fin.castLE hc) :
    ∃ (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R)
      (s : R) (h : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R),
      s ∉ p ∧
      (MvPolynomial.C s - h * Matrix.det
        (fun i j : Fin c ↦ pderiv (Fin.castLE hc i) (f j)) ∈
          Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ∧
      (∀ j, aeval P.val (f j) = 0) ∧
      Ideal.map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)))
        (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) = RingHom.ker (aeval P.val)
